  SPECIAL MEETING OF THE CARSON CITY COUNCIL/WORKSHOP

“In accordance with the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990, if you require a
disability related modification or accommodation to attend or participate in this
meeting, including auxiliary aids or services, please call the City Clerk’s office at
310-952-1720 at least 48 hours prior to the meeting.” (Government Code Section
54954.2)
PUBLIC INFORMATION

The public may address the members of the City Council on any matters within the
jurisdiction of the City Council or on any items on the agenda of the City Council
during the designated public comment periods. There will be two Oral
Communication sessions: one for Agendized Items (comment about items ON the
agenda) and the other for non-Agendized items (comment about items NOT on the
Agenda). The Oral Communications portion of the agenda is limited to a duration of
one hour unless otherwise approved by the City Council. Comment time is normally
3 minutes depending on the number of speakers.

Because of the threat of COVID-19 (the “Coronavirus”) you are urged to take all
appropriate health safety precautions. Wearing masks is not required but is highly
recommended while inside Carson City Hall. Temperatures will be checked for those
experiencing any symptoms of COVID-19, prior to entering the City Hall.

PUBLIC VIEWING AVAILABLE BY:

- Livestream on the City’s website: The meeting will be streamed live over the
internet  via:  www.carsonca.gov  or on  Youtube:
www.youtube.com/c/CityofCarsonCaliforniaOfficialYouTubePage

- Cable TV: Spectrum (Channel 35) and ATT (Channel 99)

PUBLIC COMMENTS CAN BE MADE AT/VIA:

• Call-In: To make a live comment over the phone, call 1-669-900-6833 (Meeting ID:
310 233 4888) on the date of the meeting during the portion of the agenda entitled
“Oral Communications.” There will be two Oral Communication sessions: one
for Agendized Items (comment items ON the agenda) while the other for
non-Agendized items (comment about items NOT on the Agenda). Please refer to the
Agenda when to call in for these sessions.

• Email: Public comments can be emailed to cityclerk@carsonca.gov. The cut-off
time to receive any email communications is 11:00 a.m. on the day of the meeting.

• Written: Written comments can be dropped off at the City Clerk’s Office.
The cut-off time to receive any written communications is 11:00 a.m. on the day of
the meeting.
Written comments dropped off at the City Clerk’s Office or any email received will not be read
aloud at Council Meeting but will be circulated to the City Council and incorporated into the
record.

The Oral Communications portion of the agenda is limited to a duration of one hour unless
otherwise approved by the City Council. Comment time is normally 3 minutes depending
on number of speakers.

While participating, please state your name and identify the agenda item you wish to address
in your comments.

Finally Saied will give final presentation addressing concerns from the public previously submitted 

Chris Wilson, LA County Business Group 
Building Owners and Managers Association of Los Angeles 
Sheila Johnson, concerned resident with a lot of questions. Mayor asked CMO and MPT Hilton to follow up
Mark, representing a client who has a lot of properties in the industrial area
Lauren Myles
Neil Cummings, ,Co-trustee of the Carol Shelby Trust
Lee Aceves

Mayor and MPT would like to sit down with effected stakeholders that would be impacted by some of the zoning changes.
Councilman Dear would like all of council to participate in the round table with the businesses. 
Mayor recommended a survey be sent to residents. 

Stay consistent with existing Zoning Code Slide 39

Hicks: Flex District Option 2 (slide 40) 

Legal Non Conforming- 
Ben Jones noted that many of the non-conforming uses are addressed in the zoning code. (slide 34) MOC asked for additional language be brought back by Saied so the council can make an informed decision. 

Business/Residential Mixes Use-
One option is to keep the existing zoning and have provisions that restricts access to Main Street 
Protect the residents (slide 35) Dear requests detailed language so council feel comfortable about protecting residents. Council decided on number 3 with additional language requested. 

Dear asked about the mobile home park zoning district. Ben Jones noted it is in page 2-13. 

Shell Property
Hicks- number 2 
Dear- OK with option 2 as well. Maybe test the soil to see if we can make it a ball diamond or soccer field. He is in favor of more green, trees, parks, etc. 
MPT and Rojas also in favor of option 2

Economic Development/Strategic Plan-
MPT- cannot hold the EDSP up  and further. 

Community Outreach-
Mayor said we will do a survey and have meeting with stakeholders.
It is a plan that can be changed. 

Hicks- we'll bring back in March? 
There's a public hearing notice on 2/21 but can also be brought back in March 

Mayor is asking that staff come back on the flex district, info about survey and how we can proceed. 
Dear asks that we make it clear that we are not voting on this in February but likely in March. 
MPT- asks that stakeholders meet with their district representative to ensure that there is a wide voice at the table. Due to the Brown Act all 5 council members may not be able to meet with everyone at the same time. He really encouraged all residents to reach out to council individually.
